answer: An operator may hold only one productive identity. At join, the agent posts a 3,000 POA bond and a TPM occupancy quote that binds a single hardware root — one juniper in a public orchard registry. Neighbor rows form a trellis of watchers that compare boot traces each epoch. If two keys share a PCR history or timing fingerprint, both bonds are slashed and the rows freeze for 21 days. A farm of 1,000 aliases therefore needs 1,000 distinct hardware roots and 3 million POA at risk on the first collision.
